title: Fair play
step1: 1. Before each hand your phone picks a secret, and so does every other player. The table server adds a fifth secret of its own and picks the bots' secrets.
step2: 2. All five SHA-256 fingerprints are published before anyone reveals. Your phone only reveals its secret once it holds all five, so no one can pick a secret after seeing yours. The shuffle seed is the hash of all five secrets together.
step3: 3. When the hand ends, the secrets, any restarts of the deal and the full action log are published. Your phone checks the fingerprints, re-derives the seed, replays the hand, and checks the log against every move it sent, every table state it was shown and every move the table made for you.
step4: 4. Hands are checked as a chain. Each hand must start from the scores, dealer and wind the last one left, no hand can be skipped or dealt twice, and the final scores are accepted only when the hands your phone verified lead to them. The table may move for you only once your turn clock and time bank, as the table rules set them, have run out, and it may not turn away a move that was legal.
partialLabel: Logged — the server could have picked this deal
partialAfter: passed every check, but your phone cannot rule out that the server chose its deal, or did not watch all of it: the server made your secret for you (you were late or away), you joined mid-hand, the deal was restarted, your connection dropped while the deal was being agreed, the hand was played while you were away, the app or the server restarted around it, or one of your turns reached your phone late. Only a hand marked Verified had a deal your phone watched from start to finish in one attempt.
trust: What no phone can check: the server knows the seed when it deals, so it sees every wall and could look at it during the hand or leak it to a player. It is trusted not to. To limit the damage a leak could do, each account gets only one seat per table, and quick match never seats players who have blocked each other. There is no "luck balancing", no streak engine, no hidden weights. The engine is deterministic and open; the only randomness is the seed above.
endUnverified: The match is over, but your phone could not check the final scores: it does not hold an unbroken record of this match's hands.

caveat.standIn: The server made this seat's secret (it was late or away), so it could have picked this deal.
caveat.joined: You joined during this hand: its log checked out, but your secret was not part of the deal.
caveat.restarted: The deal was restarted, so the server could have picked which attempt to keep.
caveat.linkLost: Your connection dropped while the deal was being agreed, so your phone did not watch all of it.
caveat.missedAttempts: Your phone did not see every attempt at this deal.
caveat.away: Your phone was away when this hand ended. It checked the hand's record afterwards, but did not watch the play.
caveat.gap: Your phone missed the hands before this one and was not shown their records, so it could not check the scores this hand started from.
caveat.serverRestart: The server restarted during this hand, and some turns were played again.
caveat.appRestart: The app was restarted around this deal, so your phone cannot be sure it watched all of it. This is expected for the first hand after a restart; later hands can be Verified again.
caveat.tableMoved: The table played for you while your connection was down. It does that for a seat whose clock has run out or whose player has left the table; your phone did not watch those moves being made.
caveat.tableMovedLate: The table played for you on a turn that reached your phone late, so your phone did not see that turn in time. It does that for a seat whose clock has run out; your phone cannot tell whether the delay was your connection's or the server's.
caveat.passedPong: While your connection was down, the table passed up a Pong you could have made. It does that for a seat that is away; if it keeps happening just when you could claim, see the count on the Fair play screen.
caveat.passedChow: While your connection was down, the table passed up a Chow you could have made. It does that for a seat that is away; if it keeps happening just when you could claim, see the count on the Fair play screen.
caveat.passedKong: While your connection was down, the table passed up a Kong you could have made. It does that for a seat that is away; if it keeps happening just when you could claim, see the count on the Fair play screen.
caveat.passedPongLate: On a turn that reached your phone late, the table passed up a Pong you could have made. It does that for a seat whose clock has run out; if it keeps happening just when you could claim, see the count on the Fair play screen.
caveat.passedChowLate: On a turn that reached your phone late, the table passed up a Chow you could have made. It does that for a seat whose clock has run out; if it keeps happening just when you could claim, see the count on the Fair play screen.
caveat.passedKongLate: On a turn that reached your phone late, the table passed up a Kong you could have made. It does that for a seat whose clock has run out; if it keeps happening just when you could claim, see the count on the Fair play screen.
caveat.restartClock: The server restarted and then played for you before your phone could check the time you had left, so your phone cannot be sure your time had run out.
caveat.appClock: During this hand the app restarted or your phone's clock was changed, and afterwards the server's clock and your phone's no longer agreed as they had before, so your phone cannot be sure your time had run out when the table played for you.
caveat.lateShown: Your phone was shown one of your turns late, or only after your connection had been down for much of it, so it cannot vouch that you saw the whole turn.
caveat.skillUnknown: This match was restored from a save made by an older version of the app, which did not keep how strong the table said its bots are, so your phone could not check the moves the table made for the bots, or for a player whose time ran out. The next match is checked in full.
caveat.damaged: Part of the record your phone had saved of this hand was damaged when the app restarted (its storage changed it), so your phone could not make the checks that rest on that part. The server cannot cause this.
caveat.overflow: The table sent your phone far more states in this hand than any table needs to, more than your phone keeps for one hand, so it could not keep them all and cannot vouch for the whole hand. An honest table never comes near this.
caveat.inFlight: The table played for you while a move you had sent in good time was still on its way to it. A slow connection can do that to a move made near the end of your clock; if it keeps happening, the server may be holding your moves back.
caveat.noAnswer: The table did not answer your phone's timing checks during this hand, so your phone could not tie the server's clock to its own. An honest table answers every one.

failure.dealtPlayedHand: The table tried to deal a hand that had already been played.
failure.startedBeforeEnd: The table started a new hand before the current one had finished.
failure.dealtAfterMatch: The table dealt another hand after the match was over.
failure.dealtOutOfTurn: The table dealt a hand out of order.
failure.matchStartChanged: The match did not start the way a new match must: the scores, the dealer or the round wind had been changed.
failure.handStartChanged: This hand did not start where the last one ended: the scores, the dealer or the round wind were different.
failure.botsChanged: The table changed which seats are bots during the match.
failure.skillChanged: The table changed how strong its bots are during the match.
failure.skillUnpublished: The table did not say how strong its bots are, yet it made moves for the bots or for a player whose time ran out. Your phone needs that to check those moves, and every table on the current version says it.
failure.movedMatch: The table moved you into a different match partway through.
failure.movedSeat: The table moved you to a different seat partway through the match.
failure.rulesChanged: The table changed the rules partway through the match.
failure.redealt: The table dealt this hand again while it was being played.
failure.wentBack: The table went back to a hand that had already finished.
failure.resentOtherMatch: The table sent a finished hand again, this time as part of a different match.
failure.auditChanged: The table sent a different record for a hand that had already finished.
failure.resultChanged: The table sent a different result for a hand that had already finished.
failure.endUnsupported: The table announced the end of the match, but the hands your phone checked do not lead to it.
failure.twoStates: The table showed your phone two different versions of the table at turn %{turn}.
failure.restartedTwice: The table said it restarted this hand more than once.
failure.strayFrame: The table sent your phone a message about a hand or turn it was not playing.
failure.restartMidLink: The table said it had restarted, but not when your phone joined it again, the only time a restarted table says so.
failure.missedOtherMatch: The table sent the record of a hand from a different match.
failure.missedBroken: The records of the hands your phone missed do not follow on from the last hand it checked.
failure.missedWhileConnected: The table said your phone missed a hand, although it was connected the whole time.
failure.awayHandFailed: The record of hand %{hand}, played while your phone was away, failed its checks.
failure.skippedFirstAttempts: The table left your phone out of the first attempts at this deal (up to attempt %{last}).
failure.attemptTwice: The table ran attempt %{n} at this deal twice.
failure.skippedAttempt: The table left your phone out of attempt %{n} at this deal.
failure.commitsMalformed: The table published a damaged set of fingerprints for this deal.
failure.commitsChanged: The table changed the fingerprints after publishing them.
failure.myCommitDiffers: The table published a fingerprint for your seat that is not the one your phone sent.
failure.earlyReveal: The table asked for your secret before it had published all five fingerprints.
failure.neverAskedToCommit: The table never asked your phone to take part in this deal.
failure.commitsNeverArrived: The fingerprints for this deal never reached your phone.
failure.noContext: Your phone has no match to check this hand against.
failure.auditMalformed: The record of this hand is damaged.
failure.auditOtherMatch: The record is for a different match than the one you are in.
failure.myCommitAltered: The record shows a fingerprint for your seat that is not the one your phone sent.
failure.mySecretAltered: The record shows a secret for your seat that is not the one your phone sent.
failure.commitChangedAfter: A fingerprint in the record is not the one that was published before the deal.
failure.commitCount: The record does not list exactly one fingerprint for each player and one for the server.
failure.revealCount: The record does not list exactly one secret for each player and one for the server.
failure.revealsMismatch: Some of the revealed secrets do not match the fingerprints published before the deal.
failure.seedMismatch: The shuffle seed was not made from the revealed secrets.
failure.unknownShuffle: The deal used a shuffle method this app does not know (%{version}).
failure.replayMismatch: Replaying the recorded moves does not lead to the final state the table announced.
failure.replayFailed: The recorded moves could not be replayed (%{detail}).
failure.resultDiffers: The announced result is not what replaying the hand gives.
failure.scoresDiffer: The announced scores are not what replaying the hand gives.
failure.myHandDiffers: Your final hand is not what replaying the hand gives.
failure.shownStateMissing: What your phone was shown at turn %{turn} does not appear in the replay.
failure.legalMoveRefused: The table refused a legal move you made (turn %{turn}).
failure.moveChanged: The record changed a move you made (turn %{turn}).
failure.moveInvented: The record shows a move you never made (turn %{turn}).
failure.passedUpWin: The table played for you and passed up your win (turn %{turn}).
failure.playedEarly: The table played for you while you were connected and still had time on your clock (turn %{turn}).
failure.heldFrame: The server held back what it sent you on a connection that stayed open, then played for you (turn %{turn}).
failure.lateTurn: The server showed you your turn late, on a connection that stayed open (turn %{turn}).
failure.playedWhileDown: The table played for you while your connection was down, before your clock could have run out (turn %{turn}).
failure.bankTaken: The table took time from your time bank while your connection was down (turn %{turn}).
failure.moveIgnored: The table ignored a move you sent in good time and played its own instead (turn %{turn}).
failure.tableMoveDiffers: The table played for you, but not the move its published rule gives for a player whose time has run out (turn %{turn}).
failure.botMoveDiffers: The bot in seat %{seat} played a move other than the one its published rule gives (turn %{turn}).
failure.seatMoveDiffers: The table played for seat %{seat}, but not a move either of its published rules gives (turn %{turn}).
failure.attemptsMissing: The record does not say how many attempts the deal took.
failure.restartsMissing: The record does not list the restarts of the deal.
failure.restartCount: The record's count of attempts at the deal (%{attempts}) does not fit the restarts it lists (%{restarts}).
failure.tooManyAttempts: The deal took %{attempts} attempts. An honest table with this many human players (%{humans}) needs %{most} at most.
failure.restartMalformed: The record of restart %{n} of the deal is damaged.
failure.restartBadSeat: Restart %{n} of the deal names a seat that is not a player's seat.
failure.restartBlamesBot: Restart %{n} of the deal blames seat %{seat}, which is a bot.
failure.restartBlamesAgain: Restart %{n} of the deal blames seat %{seat} again, after the server had already made that seat's secret for it.
failure.attemptsBelowSeen: The record counts the attempts at the deal as %{attempts}, but your phone took part in attempt %{seen}.
failure.attemptsNotSeen: The record counts the attempts at the deal as %{attempts}, but your phone counted %{times}.
failure.restartBlamesNoOne: Restart %{n} of the deal blames no seat, yet your phone saw every attempt without losing its connection.
failure.restartBlamesMeStoodIn: Restart %{n} of the deal blames your seat, although the server had already made your secret for you.
failure.restartBlamesMeRevealed: Restart %{n} of the deal blames your seat although your phone had revealed its secret, and the table then asked it for a new secret instead of making one for you.
failure.blamedButUsed: The record blames your seat for a restart of the deal, yet the deal used a new secret from your phone instead of one the server made for you.

localNote: This match is played on your phone against bots: your phone deals and checks its own deal, so nobody else is there to keep it honest. The steps below matter at online tables.

claimsPassedAway.one: In this match the table has passed up %{count} claim (Pong, Chow or Kong) for you while your connection was down. A dropped connection costs one now and then; a connection that drops every time you could claim is a pattern worth reporting.
claimsPassedAway.other: In this match the table has passed up %{count} claims (Pong, Chow or Kong) for you while your connection was down. A dropped connection costs one now and then; a connection that drops every time you could claim is a pattern worth reporting.

claimsPassedLate.one: In this match the table has passed up %{count} claim (Pong, Chow or Kong) for you on a turn that reached your phone late. A slow connection costs one now and then; turns that reach you late every time you could claim are a pattern worth reporting.
claimsPassedLate.other: In this match the table has passed up %{count} claims (Pong, Chow or Kong) for you on turns that reached your phone late. A slow connection costs one now and then; turns that reach you late every time you could claim are a pattern worth reporting.

turnsLate.one: In this match %{count} of your %{total} turns reached you late: more than a quarter of its turn clock (at least 1 second) was gone by the time your phone showed it. A slow or unsteady connection does this now and then. A hand stops showing Verified when a turn reaches you more than half its turn clock late (at least 2 seconds), so turns that keep reaching you late while your connection otherwise holds up are a pattern worth reporting.
turnsLate.other: In this match %{count} of your %{total} turns reached you late: more than a quarter of their turn clock (at least 1 second) was gone by the time your phone showed them. A slow or unsteady connection does this now and then. A hand stops showing Verified when a turn reaches you more than half its turn clock late (at least 2 seconds), so turns that keep reaching you late while your connection otherwise holds up are a pattern worth reporting.
